cards.text: The soldiers are leading Jesus out to be crucified. Right then, a man named Simon of Cyrene is passing by on his way in from the country. He's the father of Alexander and Rufus, and I bet this is the LAST thing he expected on his walk into town.

cards.question: The soldiers stop Simon of Cyrene. What do they force him to do?

answers.text: Lead the soldiers to the hill

cards.text: They bring Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull. There they offer Him wine mixed with myrrh.

cards.question: At Golgotha, Jesus drinks the wine mixed with myrrh.

cards.text: And they crucify Him. Then the soldiers go through His garments and split them up among themselves.

cards.question: To divide Jesus' garments, the soldiers cast ___ to decide what each of them will take.

cards.text: It's the third hour when they crucify Him. And there's a charge written out against Him.

cards.question: What does the charge written against Jesus say?

cards.text: And Jesus isn't alone up there. They crucify two other men with Him, one on His right and one on His left.

cards.question: Who are the two men crucified on either side of Jesus?

cards.text: People passing by shake their heads and heap abuse on Him. They mock Him as the One who's going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days.

cards.question: What do the people passing by dare Jesus to do?

answers.text: Come down from the cross and save Himself
Call down fire from heaven on them
Tear down the temple right now

cards.text: The chief priests and scribes join in, mocking Him among themselves: “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!” Friend, read that line one more time, slowly.

cards.question: Mocking among themselves, the chief priests and scribes say they'll believe if the Christ, the King of Israel, comes down from the cross now.
Even the men crucified with Jesus join in and berate Him.

cards.text: Then, at the sixth hour, something comes over all the land. And it stays until the ninth hour.

cards.question: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour, ___ came over all the land.

cards.text: At the ninth hour, Jesus cries out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” It means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”

cards.question: Some people standing nearby hear Jesus cry out “Eloi, Eloi.” Who do they think He's calling?

cards.text: Someone runs and fills a sponge with sour wine. He puts it on a reed and holds it up for Jesus to drink.

cards.question: As he holds up the sponge, the man says to leave Jesus alone and see if Elijah comes to take Him down.

cards.text: “But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.” Friend, take a breath with me right here.

cards.question: Jesus has breathed His last. Then the account turns to the temple. What happens there?

answers.text: The veil is torn in two

cards.question: The veil of the temple is torn from the bottom to the top.

cards.text: A Roman centurion is standing right there in front of Jesus. He sees how Jesus breathed His last, and he speaks up.

cards.question: The centurion standing in front of Jesus says, Truly this man was the ___ of God!

cards.text: The centurion isn't the only one there. There are also women watching from a distance.

cards.question: Who is one of the women watching Jesus from a distance?

cards.text: Mary Magdalene is there, along with Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.

cards.question: Mary Magdalene, the other Mary and Salome had followed Jesus and ministered to Him before. Where?

cards.text: And many other women had come up to Jerusalem with Him too. We'll stop right here for now, friend, because this story isn't finished.

findings.problem: Many story cards only restate the verse with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice: stop 1 cards 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11, and stop 2 cards 1, 5 and 14. Stop 2 card 5, for example, is the verse nearly word for word. The solemn tone suits a crucifixion passage, but these cards don't have the fatherly, teaching storyteller in them either.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Most choice cards can only be answered by luck or by already knowing the text, because the setup cards give nothing to reason from. Examples: stop 1 card 4 (whether Jesus drinks the wine), stop 1 card 10 (two robbers), stop 1 card 15 (whether the men crucified with Him berate Him), stop 2 card 2 (darkness, where the setup only says 'something comes'), stop 2 card 8 (the veil), stop 2 card 9 (top to bottom) and stop 2 card 15 (Galilee). That is more than a few discovery questions.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the exact word in 'cast ___' (lots, stones or arrows). Card 5 gives no hint about how the garments were divided, so the baker can only guess the BSB wording, not reason out its meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
